extraction.name: EgoLife
extraction.description: A comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset captured by six participants living together in a instrumented house for seven days to prepare an Earth Day celebration. It contains egocentric videos recorded via Meta Aria glasses, synchronized third-person GoPro videos, mmWave radar, and WiFi signals, along with detailed audio transcripts, visual-audio captions, and the EgoLifeQA benchmark for long-context life-oriented question answering.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Six volunteers lived together in a shared, instrumented environment (EgoHouse) for seven days in Beijing (with a supplementary 1-day session in Milan). Participants continuously wore Meta Aria glasses capturing multimodal egocentric video, audio, gaze, and IMU data for ~8 hours daily. Concurrently, 15 synchronized GoPro cameras and millimeter-wave radars (and WiFi receivers in Milan) captured third-person and spatial/movement data during daily activities.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw multimodal sensor streams: first-person video, audio, IMU, and gaze from Meta Aria glasses (stored in VRS format); third-person video from fixed GoPro cameras; raw ADC data from TI mmWave monostatic radars via DCA1000 boards; and CSI data from Asus RT-AX82U WiFi devices.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven-day period (Beijing session) and a one-day session (Milan)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Synchronization of multi-source data (Aria VRS and GoPro) via EgoSync; CFAR detection algorithm applied to mmWave ADC data to detect dynamic target signals; de-identification via EgoBlur (face blurring, bystander face blurring, license plate blurring, screen/credential masking, and muting sensitive audio segments); transcription using Whisper and speaker diarization.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts were generated using ASR (Whisper) and an open-source diarization algorithm, split into participant tracks, and human-reviewed. For captions, videos were split into 5-minute clips, slowed to 0.8x speed, and narrated verbally by annotators using CapCut, generating 361K narrations; these were merged into 25K sentences using GPT-4o-mini, enriched with sampled frames and transcripts by GPT-4o, and human-verified. For EgoLifeQA, GPT-4o generated ~100K candidate QAs across 5 categories, which annotators filtered, refined, and supplied with distractors and certification lengths to produce 3,000 final QA pairs (500 per participant).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project is ongoing; the Beijing dataset is released and annotated, while the Milan dataset and future expansions (covering broader languages, locations, and activities) are planned and documented via the EgoLife blog series.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Participant and bystander faces, personal screen contents (passwords, private data), vehicle license plates, and sensitive spoken personal topics.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables long-term egocentric AI assistants to enhance personal efficiency, assist individuals needing consistent support (e.g., the elderly or cognitively challenged), and aid learning and task tracking. Deep integration into personal spaces highlights the necessity for user privacy, ethical safeguards, and transparent decision-making.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Initial focus is intentionally narrow with limited generalizability, primarily restricted to a single living environment/scenario and predominantly Chinese language.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: EgoGPT speech understanding struggles with laughter and emotions; identity recognition is prone to overfitting to early appearance (e.g., clothing color); single-pass EgoRAG retrieval lacks multi-step reasoning and error tolerance; dataset covers a single domestic setting and primarily Chinese language in the 7-day main release.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, fine-tuning, and evaluating multimodal egocentric AI assistants, vision-audio-language models, long-term memory retrieval (RAG), and long-context question-answering across entity logging, event recall, habit insight, relationship mapping, and task management.
